metadata.title: Density Pass 37 -- 16th Vermont Counterattack (Ticks 546-560)
metadata.description: The 16th Vermont's double counterattack during Pickett's Charge -- first against Kemper's brigade threatening to roll up the Union left, then pivoting to strike Wilcox's supporting brigade. The only Union regiment to launch two separate offensive charges during the assault. Stannard's Vermont brigade acting without orders, on initiative. Often overlooked in favor of the Angle story.

placements.notes: 16th Vermont -- Stannard's fresh IX Corps brigade. They arrived yesterday and have never been in combat.
Kemper's brigade -- advancing toward Cemetery Ridge, angling left toward Stannard's position
13th Vermont -- Stannard's right regiment, watching Kemper's flank pass in front of them
16th Vermont FIRST CHARGE -- pivoting 90 degrees to strike Kemper's exposed right flank. Stannard acting without orders.
13th Vermont joining the charge into Kemper's flank -- the Vermont men are green but they are going
Kemper's brigade struck in the flank -- Kemper wounded, falling from his horse. The brigade losing cohesion.
16th Vermont having driven Kemper -- reforming. Stannard spots Wilcox's Alabama brigade advancing to support Pickett.
Wilcox's Alabama brigade advancing to support Pickett -- but Pickett is already broken, Wilcox doesn't know it yet
Lang's Florida brigade following Wilcox -- advancing into a vacuum, their objective already lost
16th Vermont SECOND CHARGE -- pivoting again, now striking Wilcox's Alabama brigade in the flank. Two charges in 8 minutes.
Wilcox hit in the flank -- Wilcox realizes Pickett has already been repulsed, orders retreat
Lang's Floridians also retreating -- they never reached the ridge
16th Vermont reforming -- two charges, two flank attacks. Their first day of combat. 76 casualties.
13th Vermont also reforming -- Stannard's brigade has helped seal the Confederate defeat
Kemper's survivors retreating -- Kemper near death from his wound. Will live until 1895.
